A half-turn quotient of the flat torus R²/(2Ze1+2Ze2), e1=(1,0),e2=(1/2,sqrt(3)/2), gives four unit equilateral faces with tetrahedral edge gluing and cone angle pi at four vertices; quotient orbital metric is min_{lambda,sign}||u±v-lambda||. Fixing u and translating v gives eccentricity as Euclidean covering radius of Lambda union (Lambda+2u). For any full-rank d>=2 torus, two open geodesic balls of radius <lambda1(Lambda)/2 are individually contractible; their union cannot cover T^d by cup-length-two obstruction (two nontrivial H¹ classes cup to nonzero H²). Thus any such two-coset cover has radius at least lambda1/2, equal to 1 here. At edge midpoint 2u=e1, the union forms rectangular lattice generated by (1,0),(0,sqrt(3)), with covering radius sqrt(1/4+3/4)=1. At a vertex 2u in Lambda, single triangular lattice covering radius 2/sqrt(3). Every source is bounded by single-coset covering and the universal lower bound; continuity and connectivity yield entire range, scaling gives a. Independently checked hexagonal and rectangular Voronoi endpoint distances; numerical generic source samples do not prove the all-source bounds.
